criteria.criterion: The study records state that teardown can reopen a backlog item rather than close it, with a citation to the pinned source path and quote.
criteria.evidence: Claims c23, c24 and c25 (claims.json) cite bin/fm-teardown.sh lines 30, 33, 39-42 and bin/fm-backlog-transition-lib.sh lines 15 and 54 at 6407052f. I read those lines in pinned-source/. They say the close is replaced by `tasks-axi reopen` while the item is still an open captain call, that mode=retain makes a replay reopen rather than close, that 'Cannot tell' refuses, and that --force does not lift the deferral. Each claim matches its source.

criteria.criterion: The study records state that with yolo on, firstmate merges green work itself, and that otherwise it does not, each with a source citation.
criteria.evidence: c26 cites AGENTS.md:234 ('with it on, firstmate merges green, in-scope work itself') and :240. c27 cites AGENTS.md:233-234 ('with it off, the captain approves every PR merge and every local-only landing'). c28 to c30 add the red-PR ban (AGENTS.md:235-236), the merge-script gates (fm-pr-merge.sh:17, fm-merge-local.sh:9-10) and the teardown lookup for a merge with no recorded PR (fm-teardown.sh:63-67). I checked every quote against the pinned lines.

criteria.criterion: The study records state that only a recorded PR or a cleanup frees a place, with citations.
criteria.evidence: c32 cites fm-project-capacity-lib.sh:48-49 ('A place therefore frees when a PR-based ship records its ready PR, or when any task is cleaned up and its record removed') and docs/configuration.md:1088. c31 (how places are counted) and c34 (a worker steered back after its PR is not counted again) cite lines 38, 45 and 51 of the same library. The clause 'Merely finishing the work frees nothing' is a fair inference from 'therefore'.

criteria.criterion: The study records separate handling of local-only ships, scouts, relaunches and secondmates, each a cited claim.
criteria.evidence: Local-only: c33, c37, c38. Scouts: c33, c39. Relaunches: c36 (fm-spawn.sh:3164-3165, matching the `$RELAUNCH -eq 0` check at line 3168) and c40. Secondmates: c35, c41 to c44 (docs/agent-control.md:72, 81, 84, 131; AGENTS.md:208; fm-teardown.sh:5, 183-184). I read every cited line and each supports its claim. One wording slip in c37 is recorded as a minor finding.

criteria.evidence: Findings: f4 covers c23 to c34 and c36 to c40, and f3 covers c35 and c41 to c44, so all of c23 to c44 are linked. Model: c23-c25 on the reopened state and t9; c26-c27 on ready and h1; c28-c29 on t10; c30, c37, c38 on t4; c31-c36 on places-held; c39 on t11; c40-c42 on t8; c43 on queued; c44 on concurrency. validation.json is byte-for-byte unchanged, but the test the_firstmate_study_passes_every_rule_against_the_pinned_tree asserts that the recorded validation equals what the rules compute now (`assert_eq!(recorded, computed)`), and it passed. findings.summary: c37 says the main local checkout 'stays with the main first mate', but the cited line says local-only projects stay with the main first mate.
findings.evidence: docs/architecture.md:336 reads '`local-only` projects stay with the main first mate because they merge into the main local checkout'. It is about which home keeps a project during secondmate seeding, not about who keeps the checkout.

findings.summary: The t9 guard leaves out that teardown's clean-worktree and landed-work gates still apply before a reopen.
findings.evidence: fm-teardown.sh:28-29 says 'None of this loosens the landed-work gates below: the transition runs only on the paths that already proceed to remove the record.' The t9 guard names only the captain-call test, so the reopen path reads as weaker than it is.

findings.summary: The change description does not name a root cause beyond saying a first reading missed these paths.
findings.evidence: f4 says 'A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths'. The CHANGELOG lists what was added but not why the first study missed it or what keeps it from happening again. The root-cause default asks for this. Work is still re-derived from source beyond the five leads (c24, c25, c29, c30, c38, c40-c44).

findings.summary: c13 still says teardown always lands a 'backlog close', which c23 qualifies, but there is no cross-reference.
findings.evidence: c13: 'Removing a task's record and landing its backlog close are one step'. c23: the close can be replaced by a reopen. This is a refinement rather than a contradiction, so no `contradicts` link is required, but a reader of c13 alone gets the old picture.

summary: The candidate passes. All five behaviours the independent reader flagged are now cited claims. They are teardown reopening an open captain call (c23-c25), yolo self-merge and the no-merge default (c26-c30), only a recorded PR or a cleanup freeing a place (c31-c34), and the separate local-only, scout, relaunch and secondmate paths (c33, c35-c44). I checked every new quote against the pinned tree at 6407052f4c521e39401ce2305dfa45d201249827, and each one supports its claim. The study adds detail the reader did not raise, such as --force not lifting the reopen, teardown's lookup for a yolo merge with no recorded PR, and how a secondmate is relaunched, recovered and retired. Every new claim is linked from the findings (f3, f4) and the model (new state `reopened`, transitions t9 to t11, and the places-held counter). validation.json is unchanged, but the kept test asserts it equals the freshly computed result, and that test passes against the mounted tree. cargo test, clippy with -D warnings, and `cargo run -p xtask -- site` all succeeded. The generated page sits outside my working directory, so I judged it from intro.json and the passing xtask render tests, not by opening the HTML. There are no blockers or major findings. Three minor ones: c37 rewords architecture.md:336 slightly wrongly; the t9 guard leaves out that teardown's landed-work gates still apply before a reopen; and the change description does not name a root cause.
